How this works

  • This email is sent once a day from your laptop.
  • You see a project here when none of its files have changed for 3 days, or when it has changes that you have not committed or pushed for 3 days.
  • Words used here: git keeps the history of your project. To commit means to save a snapshot of your changes in git. To push means to copy those snapshots online (for example to GitHub), so they are backed up.
  • Your settings file is /home/dev/second-brain/reminders.json. To stop reminders for a project for good, add its name to the "done" list. For a folder that is not a project, use the "ignore" list. To pause a project until a date, add it to "snooze" like this: "snooze": {"project-name": "2026-10-05"}.
  • The assistant did not look inside any project this time. The text comes from a quick check of file dates and git.
